chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who mortgages something with his companion, and there is no proof between them regarding it. The one holding the mortgage claimed it was for a thousand, and the owner of the mortgage said, 'It is only for one hundred.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The burden of proof is upon the one holding the mortgage that it is for a thousand; and if he does not have proof, then the oath is upon the mortgagor.'
ai.seo_question: How is a dispute over the value of a mortgage resolved in Shia jurisprudence when there is no written contract?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'Al-Bayyinah 'ala al-Mudda'i' (proof is upon the claimant) in pledge disputes, specifically addressing scenarios lacking written documentation. It clarifies that the holder of the pledge bears the burden of proof for any claimed increase in value; failing that, the mortgagor's oath prevails for the lower amount, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and evidentiary standards in commercial transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who mortgaged something with his companions. There was no proof between the two of them with regards to it. So the one with whom was the mortgaged item claimed that it was with a thousand, and the owner of the mortgaged item said, ‘But rather, it is with one hundred’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(The burden) of proof is upon the one with whom is the mortgaged item that it is with a thousand; and if there does not happen to be a proof for him, so it is upon the depositor to swear the oath’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn af-Husayn from Afi ibn ai-Hakam from ai-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Musfim who has said the following:

“It is the case of the parties of al-Rahn (security deposit) who dispute and there is no proof and testimony available for the parties involved. Al-Rahn (security deposit) holder claims it to be one thousand and the owner of al-Rahn (security deposit) claims it to be one hundred. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Al-Rahn (security deposit) holder who claims it to be one thousand is required to present proof and testimony and if he fails then the other party takes an oath.’”
